extracted.intended_audience: people researching historical Texas administrative rules (legal researchers, law students, librarians, members of the public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guide to finding historical Texas and federal administrative rules and regulations, describing primary sources (Texas Administrative Code, Texas Register), date ranges of online and print availability, and recommended research resources. Useful for locating adopted, proposed, withdrawn, and emergency rule actions and related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Administrative Code (TAC) as the compilation of state agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Administrative Code is a compilation of all state agency rules in Texas. It is continuously updated as rules are adopted or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current version published on the Texas Secretary of State's website. Use the Secretary of State TAC search feature to locate rules as they stood historically, going back to 1999. Print copies: current print copies available at the library's reference desk (1979–present); older print copies held in the library's archive and can be requested from a librarian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Register contents and role in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Register is a weekly journal of Texas state agency rulemaking that includes proposed, adopted, withdrawn and emergency rule actions; notices of state agency review of agency rules; governor's appointments; attorney general opinions; and miscellaneous documents such as requests for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After rules are adopted, they are codified and published in the Texas Administrative Code. Use the Texas Register to find non-final rule materials (proposals, notices, emergencies) and ancillary administrative documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texas Register online access and historical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: UNT's Portal to Texas History provides access to all historical versions of the Texas Register, beginning with Volume 1, No. 1 (January 6, 1976) up to within a week of the most currently released issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Texas Secretary of State Office's Texas Register search feature can locate entries in the Texas Register back to January 28, 2000. The Secretary of State also provides Texas Register indexes starting in 1997. In print availability: 1976–present; current print copies available for checkout; older print copies are held in the library's archive and can be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official search tools for historical TAC and Register entries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Secretary of State provides online search features for both the Texas Administrative Code (1999–present) and the Texas Register (searchable back to 1/28/2000), and provides indexes from 1997 onward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer official Secretary of State search interfaces for authoritative historical snapshots; use UNT Portal for comprehensive historical Texas Register scans going back to 1976.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law Handbook: Rulemaking (resource for process guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: This publication from the Texas Attorney General's Office describes Texas's rule-making process in depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this handbook to understand procedural aspects of rulemaking (how rules are proposed, noticed, adopted, and codified), which helps interpret entries in the Texas Register and TAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding Texas Regulations (Tarlton Law Library) (research guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: This guide describes how to find information in the Texas Register and the Texas Administrative Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult this guide for practical search strategies and tips specific to locating regulatory text and related materials across the Register and TAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching Texas Law: Administrative Rulemaking & Agency Procedure (Dee J. Kelly) (research guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: This guide describes how to find final Texas rules as well as non-final Texas rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for distinguishing sources for final (codified) rules vs. proposals and other non-final materials; follow its procedures to locate both types of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library disclaimer about legal advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The library cannot tell you what the law means for your situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a research reference/discovery guide only; users requiring interpretation or legal advice should consult a qualified attorney.
